Both are minimal and required to unblock B-5a88's own DEV to REVIEW scope gate and its CHK-003/CHK-012 DONE-required pinned test. (1) packages/main/src/core/finding-verify.ts: the B-cc10 state-dir migration orphaned the entire historical B-META gap-log provenance chain, so classifySharedLifecycleMetadata reported those shared paths as untrusted and the scope gate refused this story's merge-imported B-META change with invalid_binding_shape. Two read-only compatibility fixes: committedArtifactDigest now probes stateDirCandidates canonical-first instead of the canonical literal alone, and the per-receipt loop accepts either state-dir spelling for the signed artifactPath/ledgerPath fields, which pre-migration receipts cannot rewrite without invalidating their own HMAC. No weakening: resolved bytes must still digest to the recorded preArtifactDigest and the HMAC/sequence/digest checks are unchanged; new writes still emit only the canonical spelling. artifact-schema-migration.test.mjs already asserted this either-spelling tolerance, so this aligns the verifier with its stated contract. Verified: verifyGapLogArtifactBinding now returns valid_official_gap_log_binding, gap_log works again repo-wide after refusing every write all session, and the pinned test passes. (2) B-5a88-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md: durable traceable record of three defects deliberately NOT fixed here, each with repro steps, evidence, blast radius and recommended handling, following the repo's existing B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md precedent.

Both files carry the fix for a real regression THIS story introduced, so they are in-scope repair rather than scope expansion. CHK-007 correctly narrowed PROOF_OR_STOP_BIN_NAMES to the canonical pair so retired lattice names are never advertised in usage text, but two PARSER call sites reused that same list to strip a redundant bin token pasted as argv[0], so 'lattice host runtime list' regressed to 'Unknown command: lattice'. That regression was caught by cli-surface-smoke, a configured validate command, and both call sites' own comments state they forgive a pasted bin token under EITHER name, so the narrowing contradicted their documented contract. Fix adds an exported STRIPPABLE_BIN_TOKENS (canonical union retired) in cli/alias-normalizer.ts consumed only by those two parser sites, mirroring the established BIN_TOKEN_ALTERNATION union in core/audit-scan.ts. Parse-tolerating a token does not advertise it: resolveUsageBin still gates strictly on PROOF_OR_STOP_BIN_NAMES, bin-alias-migration.test.mjs (CHK-007's own test) passes, verify-lattice-residue npm-bin passes, and cli.js help emits zero lattice bin forms. cli-engine.ts additionally drops the dead PROOF_OR_STOP_BIN_NAMES import that the fix left behind (finding F-502, filed by the concept lane and now resolved). All three reviewer lanes reviewed these exact files this round; concept and quality each independently verified the advertising path is untouched.

Shared dev-memory experience log, written by the framework's own dev_memory_capture command whose output the DONE gate requires: story_advance DONE refuses with [missing_dev_memory_finish_decision] until a finish decision exists, and this story honestly recorded decision=captured rather than taking the no-reusable-lesson exit, because the convergence produced two genuinely reusable lessons. Entry 12f5957 (failure-mode) records that a DONE-required receipt written by a separate process self-invalidates through its own metadata auto-commit, so only done_prepare's single-process write-and-consume converges; it also lists the three hypotheses that were disproven by test so the next reader does not repeat them. Entry d9398e6 (tool-quirk) records that the CertificationWindow needs a FINALIZED UNCONSUMED review-inventory receipt while story_advance --phase=DEV consumes it, which is why three receipts were spent before the pattern was seen. Content is append-only lesson text with no product-runtime effect; the file is a cross-story shared log, not B-5a88-owned source, so it falls outside the story's declared path set by construction rather than by scope creep.
